description: From the Channel coast to Provence, Rick deliberately leaves the best-known French routes to find regional cooks, producers and dishes in Normandy, Picardie, Alsace, Burgundy, Auvergne, Périgord, Languedoc, Roussillon and the Mediterranean south.

s10e01.description: Rick starts around Dieppe with turbot and the Channel coast, then follows the Bay of Somme's edible sea herbs and the food traditions of Picardie and Champagne away from the obvious tourist circuit.

s10e02.description: Along France's eastern border, Alsace, the Jura and Burgundy provide choucroute garnie, Comté and a succession of deeply regional foods shaped by mountains, vineyards and neighbours across the frontier.

s10e03.description: Rick moves from Burgundy into the Auvergne, concentrating on the meat, dairy, charcuterie and farmhouse cooking of central France rather than the polished restaurant version exported abroad.

s10e04.description: Périgord is treated as a working food landscape of truffles, walnuts and duck, with Rick cooking enchaud, a slow roast of pork, before continuing south through rural France.

s10e05.description: The route reaches French Catalonia, the Pyrenees and the Mediterranean, where Languedoc and Roussillon combine mountain produce, coastal fish and a culinary identity distinct from northern France.

s10e06.description: The journey finishes in Provence and around Cassis, where Mediterranean vegetables, fish and olive oil culminate in dishes such as a tomato and aubergine tarte tatin.
